title: The West Is Thinking Too Small About Ukraine's Victory
gist: Alanna Novetsky argues the West treats Ukraine's war with short-term crisis responses and 'one weird trick' thinking, while Russia's winter attacks on infrastructure target societal endurance; victory is a generational project, and Western partners should replicate drone co-production models in education, health and other sectors.

insights.claim: Since fall 2023, Ukraine's supporters have repeated an annual cycle of warnings about attacks on the energy grid, insufficient hardening aid, Ukrainian improvisation, and relief at spring, which shows a fundamentally short-term Western view.
insights.speaker: Alanna Novetsky
insights.so_what: Expect underinvestment in infrastructure resilience ahead of each winter.

insights.claim: Western policy falls into crisis response ('Something must be done!') or 'one weird trick' thinking, both built on easy levers such as statements, sanctions, aid packages and meetings that do not match Russia's grinding strategy.
insights.speaker: Alanna Novetsky
insights.so_what: Sanction and aid headlines are unlikely to end the war by themselves.
insights.locator: The West's approach to Ukraine often falls

insights.claim: Russia's repeated fall strikes have hit warehouses with more than 8 million children's books, data centers and mobile providers, trains between Poland and Ukraine, and bridges between Moldova and Ukraine.
insights.speaker: Alanna Novetsky
insights.so_what: Targeting spans logistics and connectivity, not just power, raising risk to cross-border links.
insights.locator: Look at some of the targets

insights.claim: Chronic school disruption for nearly five million children pulls parents away from work, harms the Ukrainian economy, and pushes families to leave.
insights.speaker: Alanna Novetsky
insights.so_what: Demographic and labor erosion are slow-burning risks for Ukraine's economy and reconstruction.

insights.claim: The author argues Russia could debilitate the Ukrainian state by straining core institutions even if it cannot win on the battlefield.
insights.speaker: Alanna Novetsky
insights.so_what: Non-battlefield institutional strain is an underweighted risk in Ukraine outcomes.

insights.claim: Victory for Ukraine will take a generation and will be determined by today's young Ukrainians defending borders, rebuilding, and revitalizing democracy and economy.
insights.speaker: Alanna Novetsky
insights.so_what: Investment horizons for Ukraine should be decades, not winter-to-winter.
insights.locator: Victory for Ukraine will take a generation

insights.claim: Ukraine's defense ministry has created pathways for European allies, most famously Denmark, to co-produce weapons with Ukraine's most effective firms, and the author says this model of direct interest in specific firms should be replicated across other sectors.
insights.speaker: Alanna Novetsky
insights.so_what: Co-production deals are a template for Western capital into Ukraine; watch for equivalents in education, health and energy.
insights.locator: Ukraine's ministry of defense has created pathways

insights.claim: Mariupol State University, operating in exile in Kyiv, reaches students in occupied territories and its rector Mykola Trofymenko became deputy minister of education and science in 2025; the author cites it as an underfunded model institution.
insights.speaker: Alanna Novetsky
insights.so_what: Example of undercapitalized resilience solutions that partners could fund.
insights.locator: Take, for example, Mariupol State University
